solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very wet day considered fit for the family?

parts.note: SAT is the short form of Saturday
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all the family
rated means judged or considered

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rainy day out is suitable for the whole family.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone, so a U-rated film is fit for the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaked through, holding all the water it can, is very wet.

clue.text: Getting thin wood cut up is a piece of cake, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the shortened word is read from the bottom upwards
cut means the wood's name loses its final letter

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood, sold in thin sheets for models

explanation.surface: Slicing thin wood is supposedly easy, a piece of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' tempts as the idiom for something easy; here it is a literal piece of cake, a thick slice.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick flat chunk cut from a cake can be called a slab, an example rather than a synonym, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Scene captured by Constable audaciously

indicators.note: captured by says the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A landscape scene painted boldly by the artist John Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque grouping or scene, especially one posed or depicted.

clue.text: Unpleasant character reacts oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word reacts

explanation.surface: A nasty person responds in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a contemptible, treacherous person.

clue.text: Flog rubbish outside front of Harrods

indicators.note: outside says the word for rubbish goes around the next letter

parts.note: trash is rubbish

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of the store's name

explanation.surface: Someone sells junk outside the famous London department store.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrods is a famous London department store. 'Flog' looks like British slang for sell, but here it means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat with a whip or stick, which is what thrashing means.

clue.text: Absolutely depressed? Correct

parts.note: down means depressed or low in spirits
right means correct

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are utterly depressed and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means thoroughly or utterly, as in downright rude.

clue.text: Drink friend knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for friend is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend downs a drink in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking quickly, but signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap is to drink by scooping liquid with the tongue, as a cat does.

clue.text: End of motorway having illumination all round

indicators.note: all round says the lighting word surrounds the motorway

parts.note: lit means illuminated, lighting up
M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: The end of a motorway is lit up all around.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or furthest point, the end beyond which one cannot go.

clue.text: Ask questions as insect gets inside food store

indicators.note: gets inside says the insect is placed within the word for asking questions

parts.note: to pry is to ask nosy questions
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect sneaks into the larder, prompting questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard where food is kept.

clue.text: Judge prepared rarebit

indicators.note: prepared, as food is made ready, signals the letters of rarebit rearranged

explanation.surface: A cookery judge has made Welsh rarebit, cheese on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes or decides, a judge.

clue.text: Old maidens in novel about females

indicators.note: in says these letters go within the turned word
about says the word for novel is turned around

parts.note: novel means new
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Elderly unmarried women feature in a novel about women.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: Women are adult female people, so a plain synonym for females.

clue.text: It's a vehicle used by car salesmen, one protests

definitions.text: a vehicle used by car salesmen
definitions.meaning: a car kept by a dealer for test drives
someone who takes part in a public protest

explanation.surface: A car dealer's vehicle is apparently also someone who protests.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer's test-drive car is a demonstration model, and a protester is one who demonstrates.

clue.text: One working under dodgy bosses reveals hang-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the following letters below the rest
dodgy means unsound, so the letters of bosses are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A worker with shady bosses discloses a psychological problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' turns BOSSES into OBSESS; 'under' puts I and ON beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is a fixation or persistent preoccupation, an obsession.

clue.text: Mad for fruit

definitions.meaning: hard-shelled seeds such as walnuts or hazelnuts

explanation.surface: Someone is crazy about fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for crazy and also names hard-shelled fruits like hazelnuts.

clue.text: Floor covering turned over by university teacher

indicators.note: turned over says the floor covering is read backwards

parts.note: a rug covers a floor

explanation.surface: A university lecturer flips over a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a spiritual teacher or revered mentor, originally in Hinduism.

clue.text: Regimental leader, say, at army's sporting event

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of the word Regimental

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A regiment's commander attends an army sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat or yacht races, a sporting event on water.

clue.text: Guard foreign sector

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters of sector are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers protect an overseas zone.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a person or group accompanying someone for protection, a guard.

clue.text: Dear writer of verses has penned two pages

indicators.note: has penned says the writer encloses the pages, like a pen enclosing animals

parts.note: a poet writes verses
PP is the abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: A beloved poet has written a couple of pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is an affectionate British term for a sweet person, like dear or darling.

clue.text: Mostly posh explorer wants time in North London suburb

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word for posh

parts.note: swish means smart and posh
Robert Falcon Scott was the British Antarctic explorer
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A posh explorer wants to spend time in a smart part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a district of north London, named after a chalet-style inn.
explanation.definitionFit: This district lies in Camden, in north London, a residential area.

clue.text: European country, I agree, needing to expel one Liberal

indicators.note: needing to expel says one letter is removed from the word for agree

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A politician agrees a country must throw out a Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: French cheese that is inferior to British

indicators.note: in a down clue, inferior to means placed below

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a French cheese is worse than a British one.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft cow's-milk cheese from France.

clue.text: Somewhat romantic person from the Middle East

indicators.note: somewhat is meant to say only part of the word romantic is used, but the part needed is not one unbroken run

explanation.surface: A rather romantic person comes from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: A flawed clue: 'Somewhat' was meant to hide the answer in ROMANTIC, but the T sits between OMAN and I, so the letters only come by dropping R, T and C, which no fair indicator signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or citizen of Oman, a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula, is called this.

clue.text: Talk of salesman carrying large serving dish

indicators.note: carrying says the sales talk holds the size letter

parts.note: patter is a salesman's glib talk

explanation.surface: A salesman's spiel accompanies a big serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large flat plate for serving food.

clue.text: Enjoying good 'ealth drink

indicators.note: the dropped h of 'ealth, a Cockney pronunciation, tells us to drop the first letter of the word for healthy

parts.note: hale means in good health, robust

explanation.surface: A healthy drink, spoken in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney (London working-class) speech drops initial H, as in 'ealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is beer, an alcoholic drink brewed from malt.

clue.text: Conservative rejects zero tax

indicators.note: rejects says the zero is thrown out of the party word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician refuses a zero-rate tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax is to strain or test, as in trying one's patience.

clue.text: No Communist will enter boring cathedral

indicators.note: will enter says the Communist goes inside the word for boring

parts.note: tame means dull or boring
a Red is a Communist

explanation.surface: No Communist would visit a dull cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Notre Dame is the Gothic cathedral in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The name refers to the famous Gothic cathedral in Paris and others like it.
